project.name: Hospital Management System
project.summary: A system for patient registration, appointment scheduling, medical record access, doctor workflow, and admin billing.

functional_requirements: Patients can register and maintain personal profiles.
Patients can book, modify, and cancel appointments with doctors.
Patients can view their own medical history and prescription records.
Doctors can manage their appointment schedules and record diagnoses.
Administrators can manage departments, doctors, and patient billing.
non_functional_requirements: All patient data must be stored and transmitted securely following HIPAA guidelines.
System responses for user actions must be under 2 seconds.
The system must achieve 99.9% uptime and support failover.
The architecture should be scalable to handle peak loads of 10,000 concurrent users.

actors.name: Patient
actors.description: Registers, books appointments, and accesses personal medical information.

actors.name: Doctor
actors.description: Manages schedule, records diagnoses, and writes prescriptions for patients.

actors.name: Administrator
actors.description: Oversees departments, doctor accounts, and handles patient billing.

use_cases.name: Register Account
use_cases.description: Creates a new user profile with personal and contact details.

use_cases.name: Book Appointment
use_cases.description: Selects a doctor and time slot, then confirms the appointment.

use_cases.name: View Medical History
use_cases.description: Retrieves a list of past visits, diagnoses, and prescriptions.

use_cases.name: Record Diagnosis and Prescription
use_cases.description: Enters diagnosis details and generates a prescription linked to the patient record.

use_cases.name: Manage Billing
use_cases.description: Creates, updates, and exports invoices for patient services.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Patients can register and maintain personal profiles.
criteria: Registration succeeds only when all mandatory fields are provided.
A confirmation email is sent to the patient after successful registration.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Patients can book, modify, and cancel appointments with doctors.
criteria: The system prevents double‑booking of the same time slot.
Patients receive a notification confirming the booked, modified, or cancelled appointment.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Patients can view their own medical history and prescription records.
criteria: Only the authenticated patient can access their records.
Medical history loads within 2 seconds for any query.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Doctors can manage their appointment schedules and record diagnoses.
criteria: Doctors can add, edit, or remove appointments in their personal calendar.
Diagnoses and prescriptions are saved and immediately visible in the patient’s record.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Administrators can manage departments, doctors, and patient billing.
criteria: Admins can generate an invoice for a patient’s visit with correct charges.
Invoices can be exported as PDF files.

user_stories.story: As a patient, I want to register an account, so that I can access the hospital system securely.
acceptance_criteria: Patient can create an account with email and password.
System validates required fields and stores encrypted credentials.

user_stories.story: As a patient, I want to book appointments with doctors, so that I can receive timely care.
acceptance_criteria: Patient can view available time slots for selected doctor.
Appointment is confirmed and added to both patient and doctor schedules.

user_stories.story: As a patient, I want to view my medical history, so that I can stay informed about my health.
acceptance_criteria: Patient can access a list of past visits, diagnoses, and prescriptions.
Data is displayed only after successful authentication.

user_stories.story: As a doctor, I want to manage my appointment schedule, so that I can organize my patient visits efficiently.
acceptance_criteria: Doctor can view, add, modify, and cancel appointments.
Schedule changes are reflected in real-time for patients.

user_stories.story: As a doctor, I want to record diagnoses and write prescriptions, so that patients receive appropriate treatment.
acceptance_criteria: Doctor can enter diagnosis details and select medications from a formulary.
Prescriptions are saved to the patient’s record and can be viewed by the patient.

user_stories.story: As an administrator, I want to manage departments, doctors, and patient billing, so that the hospital operates smoothly.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can add, edit, or remove departments and assign doctors to them.
Admin can generate and update billing records for patient services.

Database Designer.sql:
CREATE TABLE Patients (
    patient_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    dob DATETIME,
    phone TEXT,
    address TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE Doctors (
    doctor_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    specialty TEXT,
    phone TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE Appointments (
    appointment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    patient_id INTEGER,
    doctor_id INTEGER,
    appointment_time DATETIME,
    status TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (patient_id) REFERENCES Patients(patient_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (doctor_id) REFERENCES Doctors(doctor_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Prescriptions (
    prescription_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    appointment_id INTEGER,
    medication TEXT,
    dosage TEXT,
    notes TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (appointment_id) REFERENCES Appointments(appointment_id)
);

Project Structure.architecture: Microservice‑style deployment with a single FastAPI service handling authentication, patient, doctor and admin domains, a PostgreSQL relational store, Redis for caching and session tokens, and a React/Vite SPA served via Nginx. Docker containers ensure portability and high availability; Kubernetes can orchestrate scaling and health checks.
Project Structure.architecture_diagram:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Client
        A[React SPA] --> B[Axios API Calls]
    end
    subgraph Server
        B --> C[FastAPI]
        C --> D[PostgreSQL]
        C --> E[Redis]
    end
    subgraph Infra
        F[Nginx] --> A
        G[Docker Compose]
        G --> C
        G --> D
        G --> E
    end

Documentation.readme: Hospital Management System (HMS) enables patient registration, appointment booking, medical history viewing, doctor schedule management, diagnosis recording, prescription writing, and admin control of departments, staff, and billing. Built with a RESTful API, React frontend, Node.js/Express backend, and PostgreSQL database. Emphasizes data security, low latency, and 99.9% uptime.
Documentation.api_documentation: POST /patients – register; GET /patients/{id} – profile; GET /patients/{id}/history – medical history. POST /appointments – book; GET /doctors/{id}/schedule – view schedule; PUT /appointments/{id} – update status. POST /diagnoses – record; POST /prescriptions – create. Admin: GET/POST/PUT /departments, /doctors, /billing. All endpoints require JWT auth, role‑based access.
Documentation.installation: Clone repo, run `npm install` in server and client directories. Set up PostgreSQL, run `psql -f schema.sql`. Create .env with DB_URL, JWT_SECRET, and PORT. Run `npm run migrate` to apply migrations. Start server with `npm start` and client with `npm run dev`.
Documentation.deployment: Containerize with Docker; use docker-compose to launch app, db, and reverse proxy (NGINX). Deploy to cloud (AWS ECS, Azure AKS, or GCP GKE). Enable TLS via Let's Encrypt. Configure auto‑scaling and health checks for high availability.
Documentation.sprint_plan: Sprint 1: Core patient registration & auth. Sprint 2: Appointment booking & doctor schedule UI. Sprint 3: Diagnosis, prescription APIs. Sprint 4: Admin module for departments, billing. Sprint 5: Security hardening, JWT refresh, audit logs. Sprint 6: Performance testing, CI/CD pipeline, documentation.
Documentation.architecture: Three‑tier: React SPA (frontend) → Node.js/Express REST API (business logic) → PostgreSQL (data). JWT for stateless auth, role‑based middleware. NGINX as reverse proxy and load balancer. Docker containers for each tier, orchestrated by Docker Compose or Kubernetes. Logging with Winston, monitoring via Prometheus/Grafana.
